subject: Incorporating UTF8 characters in a text string

messages.author: 23e9c489ea8b313a
messages.subject: Incorporating UTF8 characters in a text string
parts:
I am preparing a simple probability calculator for an introductory class.  One version is at the inappropriately named

http://bates.shinyapps.io/normalDensity

It started out as creating a normal density curve with a shaded area, then grew.  Shiny makes things easy to generalize.

I want to use the "less than or equal to", ≤ character instead of '<' in "P(X < x) = " but I can't work out how to do that.  Sources are at

https://github.com/dmbates/normalDensityApp/

I would appreciate suggestions on how to accomplish this.

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating UTF8 characters in a text string
parts:
On my Mac, it works for me if I just put the character directly in the string. For example:

runApp(list(
  ui = bootstrapPage(
    numericInput('n', 'N', 100),
    verbatimTextOutput('textout')
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$textout <- renderText({ paste(input$n, "≤ ∞") })
  }
))


-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Incorporating UTF8 characters in a text string
parts:
You can use html like this:

    output$probstring <- renderUI({ 
      string <- "Normal P(X<x)=0.8483"
      HTML(sub("<", " ≤ ", string))
    })

and in ui.R use uiOutput() instead of verbatimTextOutput().

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating UTF8 characters in a text string
parts:
Stephane - instead of including the UTF-8 character directly, you can also specify Unicode values in strings with something like "\U2264". The string "\U2264 \U221E" is equivalent to "≤ ∞", and it can be read more reliably across platforms.

The result is the same (again, on my Mac):
> "\U2264 \U221E"
[1] "≤ ∞"
> "≤ ∞"
[1] "≤ ∞"


Does this app work for you in Windows?

runApp(list(
  ui = bootstrapPage(
    numericInput('n', 'N', 100),
    verbatimTextOutput('textout')
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

output$textout <- renderText({ paste(input$n, "\U2264 \U221E") })
  }
))

-Winston

parts:
> x <- paste("a", "\U2264 \u221E")
> # it works in the console:
> x
[1] "a ≤ ∞"
> Encoding(x)
[1] "UTF-8"
> # but in the browser, we exactly see this:
